checklist.notes: The minimal-pair goal is suitable for A1.1, but directions such as ‘farther forward’, ‘one-vowel change alters the message’, ‘without viewing the speaking list’, ‘reset the tongue position’, and ‘intended word’ are substantially above unsupported A1.1 comprehension.
The /ɪ/–/iː/ contrast is not reduced to duration alone, and the qualified articulatory description is reasonable across common teaching models. The example word forms are accurate.
The clarification exchange is intelligible, but its echo question is deliberately contrived and under-contextualized; that local issue is recorded as minor.
No suspicious unexplained overlap appeared within the supplied request and ten-lesson set. The check cannot establish external originality.
The lesson uses minimal-pair discrimination and spoken interaction while relying only on previously established phoneme, listening, and speaking capabilities.
The content is in English and all embedded references fall inside the exact request or its context-only prerequisite closure.

methods: Manual comparison of lesson wording with the supplied authoritative request and project-authored teaching payload.
Exact contiguous-word overlap comparison across the ten supplied v3 lesson bodies.
Inspection of the accepted audit provenance/copyright scope without consulting external sources.
copyright_originality_check.scope_limitations: No suspicious unexplained copying was found within the supplied scope. Reuse of target forms, short pedagogical frames, and project-authored definitions/examples is expected. No external search was performed; this is not a plagiarism clearance or copyright guarantee.

findings.description: Across all four sections, essential production and self-check instructions use abstract vocabulary and multi-clause syntax beyond A1.1 without glosses or L1 support. A beginner may understand live/leave but not the procedure used to practise or assess the contrast.
findings.recommendation: Replace the prose with short numbered commands using high-frequency words and demonstrations; gloss or translate unavoidable mouth-position terms.

findings.description: The heading calls the exchange natural, but the bare echo ‘Leave here?’ is semantically under-specified and sounds more like a constructed minimal-pair prompt than an ordinary clarification.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit repair turn such as ‘Did you say leave?’ / ‘No, live,’ while retaining the vowel contrast.

limitations: Review used only the exact lesson, accepted audit, regenerated hash-matching authoritative request, and verified M5 development snapshot; generator reasoning and prior review records were excluded.
No audio was supplied; pronunciation judgments cover written instructions and IPA only, not realized speech or learner performance.
No external CEFR vocabulary profiler or corpus was used; CEFR findings are qualitative independent AI judgments about the learner-facing text.

Originality checking was limited to the supplied authoritative payload and the ten supplied v3 lessons; no Internet, external corpus, or plagiarism search was performed, so no external plagiarism or legal-clearance claim is made.
